experiments.name: Support Triage — SaaS Ticket Router
experiments.description: Evaluate billing, technical issues, urgency, escalation and churn risk independently in support tickets.

is_billing_issue.instructions: Is this ticket about billing, payments, invoices, charges, refunds, or subscription/pricing?

is_technical_issue.instructions: Is this ticket reporting a technical bug, error, outage, or product not working as expected?

is_urgent.instructions: Does this ticket indicate urgency — service down, blocking work, or customer explicitly says urgent/ASAP?

needs_escalation.instructions: Should this ticket be escalated to engineering or a senior agent (not solvable by L1 support)?

is_churn_risk.instructions: Does this message suggest the customer may cancel or churn (mentions leaving, competitor, very frustrated, 'last chance')?

examples: Hi team, our production API has been returning 500 errors for the last 45 minutes and our customers are affected. This is blocking our launch — need urgent escalation to engineering. We're considering alternatives if not fixed today.
Hello, I was charged twice on my invoice #INV-8842 for $299. The duplicate charge appeared yesterday. Can you please refund the extra payment? Account: acme-corp@acme.com
Hey, I can't log in since the password reset yesterday. I tried clearing cache and different browsers. It's not urgent, just my account. Thanks for checking when you have time.
We've been happy for 2 years but this is the third billing error this quarter. If this isn't resolved and compensated, we'll need to evaluate other vendors before renewal next month.

experiments.name: Email Threat Detection
experiments.description: Evaluate phishing signals, suspicious links or requests, and legitimate correspondence in sample emails.

is_phishing.instructions: Is this email a phishing attempt, scam, or deceptive message trying to steal credentials, money, or sensitive info?

has_malicious_link_or_request.instructions: Does this email contain a suspicious link, attachment, urgent wire-transfer request, or asks to verify account via clicking?

is_safe_legitimate.instructions: Is this a normal legitimate personal or work email without deception or threat?

examples:
Subject: Action Required: Verify your Microsoft 365 account

Dear user, your mailbox is almost full. Click here to verify within 24h or your account will be suspended: http://microsof-365-secure-login.com/verify

Subject: Wire transfer needed

Hi Sarah, per our CEO's request, please wire $48,500 to account 987654321 by EOD. This is confidential. — John (CFO) — Sent from my iPhone

Subject: Lunch tomorrow? 

Hey Alex, are we still on for lunch tomorrow at 12:30 near the downtown cafe? Let me know if you need to reschedule. — Priya

Subject: Invoice #4829 Overdue

Hi team, friendly reminder that invoice #4829 for $1,200 is due next week. Let me know if you have any questions. Best, accounting@vendor.com

experiments.name: Trust & Safety — Content Moderation
experiments.description: Evaluate toxicity, harassment, spam and self-harm signals against the supplied questions.

is_toxic.instructions: Does this content contain toxic language, hate, severe profanity, or personal attacks?

is_harassment.instructions: Does this content harass, bully, threaten, dox, or target a specific person or group?

is_spam.instructions: Is this content spam, unsolicited promotion, scam, or repetitive low-quality promotion?

is_self_harm.instructions: Does this content express self-harm, suicidal ideation, or disordered eating intent?

is_safe.instructions: Is this content safe, benign, and appropriate for a general audience with no policy violation?

examples: You are a worthless idiot and everyone knows it. Go away and never post again — you're a waste of space.
Hey everyone! Check my new crypto giveaway — click bit.ly/freecoins now to get $500 free!!! Limited time!!!
I can't do this anymore. I feel hopeless and have been thinking about ending it. Is anyone there?
Great article! I found the section on caching very helpful. Perhaps you could also cover Redis vs Memcached differences in the next post?

experiments.name: 911 Emergency Dispatch Router
experiments.description: Explore routing signals in fictional emergency transcripts. This demonstration is not an operational dispatch system.

is_fire_emergency.instructions: Is this an emergency involving fire, smoke, gas leak, explosion, or burn risk needing Fire Dept?

is_medical_emergency.instructions: Is this a medical emergency needing ambulance — person injured, unconscious, chest pain, bleeding, or struggling to breathe?

is_police_emergency.instructions: Is this an emergency involving crime, violence, weapons, intrusion, or immediate police need?

has_multiple_victims.instructions: Does this emergency involve multiple people hurt, trapped, or in danger (not just one person)?

caller_in_immediate_danger.instructions: Is the caller themselves currently in immediate physical danger or trapped?

examples: Operator, there's a fire in the warehouse on 4th and Main — thick black smoke, alarms going off, I'm still inside with two coworkers near the loading dock, we can't get to the exit!
My husband is 58, collapsed in the kitchen, he's unconscious and not breathing properly, his face looks pale — please send an ambulance fast, address is 1420 Oak Drive.
There's an armed man in the corner store on Elm Street threatening the cashier with a gun, customers are on the floor — please send police immediately!
My neighbor's carbon monoxide alarm is beeping and she feels dizzy and nauseous, the whole apartment smells like gas — we evacuated but she's still feeling sick.

experiments.name: Code Review Guard — PR Risk
experiments.description: Evaluate code changes for secrets, dangerous operations and other review risks.

breaks_api_contract.instructions: Does this code change break a public API or contract in a backward-incompatible way (renamed/removed endpoint, changed response shape without versioning)?

has_secret_leak.instructions: Does this change introduce a hardcoded secret, API key, password, token, or credentials in code or config?

dangerous_operation.instructions: Does this change include a dangerous operation like mass deletion (rm -rf), unvalidated shell execution, raw SQL from user input, or destructive DB migration?

has_disabled_tests.instructions: Does this change disable, skip, comment out, or delete tests to make CI pass without fixing underlying issues?

examples: PR: Changed GET /api/v1/users to GET /api/users and removed the v1 backward-compatibility shim. All clients must migrate immediately.
PR: Added config.py line: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = 'sk_live_51H7x8...production_key_here' and committed to repo.
PR: Added utils/cleanup.py: os.system('rm -rf ' + user_supplied_path) without any validation or sanitization, called from API endpoint.
PR: Deleted 42 failing tests and added @pytest.mark.skip to 18 more to 'unblock CI' before release.

experiments.name: Finance — Invoice Risk Review
experiments.description: Evaluate fictional invoices for discrepancies and review signals.

has_missing_fields.instructions: Does this invoice lack required fields — missing vendor, invoice number, date, line items, or total?

has_amount_mismatch.instructions: Is there an amount mismatch — line items sum doesn't equal total, tax miscalc, or currency inconsistency?

is_likely_duplicate.instructions: Is this likely a duplicate invoice — same vendor, invoice number, date and amount as a prior invoice?

needs_manual_review.instructions: Should this invoice be flagged for manual human review due to risk, anomaly, or policy exception?

examples: Invoice INV-2024-0842 | Vendor: Acme Supplies | Date: 2024-09-10 | Line: 100x Widgets @ $5 = $500 | Total: $750 (no tax/shipping breakdown, total mismatch)
Invoice from Global Parts — no invoice number, no date, just a total $12,400 with a note 'for services' and a bank account for wire transfer.
Invoice INV-8891 | Vendor: OfficeMax | Date: 2024-08-15 | Total: $1,200 | Note: This is the second submission of INV-8891 same date/amount (already paid Aug 15).
Invoice INV-7721 | Vendor: TechParts Inc | Date: 2024-09-12 | Line items: 2× Server @ $3000 = $6000, Tax: $480 (8%), Shipping: $0, Total: $6480 — all fields present and math checks out.

experiments.name: E-commerce Sentiment & Review
experiments.description: Evaluate positive, negative and neutral sentiment in product reviews.

positive.instructions: Does this text express positive sentiment, praise, delight, or satisfaction about the product/service?

negative.instructions: Does this text express negative sentiment, disappointment, complaint, or dissatisfaction?

neutral.instructions: Is this text neutral, factual, mixed, or neither clearly positive nor negative?

examples: Absolutely love this coffee machine! The build quality is fantastic, it heats up in 20 seconds and the crema is perfect every time. Best purchase I've made this year — 5 stars, will recommend to friends.
Ordered the headphones and they arrived with a broken hinge. Customer support took 5 days to reply and offered only a partial refund. Very disappointed for a $199 product.
The package arrived on time. The item looks as described. I haven't used it extensively yet, so I can't comment on durability — it's okay for now, does the job.
This product is amazing! Best purchase ever — exceeded expectations on every front and support was stellar.
